headline: Analysis Reveals Omnicorp Holdings Properties Form 'Perfect Geometric Pattern' Across City
subheadline: Amateur cartographer discovers shell company's 47 properties create shape visible only from above
summary: A mapping project has revealed that properties owned by the mysterious Omnicorp Holdings form a deliberate geometric pattern when viewed from satellite imagery.
content:
Omnicorp Holdings owns the Hartwell Building. Everyone knows that. What nobody knew until last week: they own 46 other properties across the city, and together they form a shape.

Amateur cartographer and urban planning enthusiast u/MapperMayhem discovered the pattern while researching property ownership for an unrelated project.

"I was tracking shell company ownership to understand development patterns," they explained. "Omnicorp came up a lot. So I plotted all their properties on a map. And then I zoomed out."

The 47 properties—warehouses, vacant lots, one apartment building, a defunct radio station, and the Hartwell Building at the center—form a perfect spiral when connected in order of purchase date.

"The math is exact," wrote u/MapperMayhem. "This is a logarithmic spiral. The Hartwell Building is at the focal point. The purchases span from 1952 to 2024, and each one follows the spiral precisely. This wasn't accidental. Someone planned this over 72 years."

The pattern has attracted attention from the Hartwell Files community, which has long investigated the building's anomalies.

"We always knew Omnicorp was hiding something," wrote Chen Wei, who runs the @HartwellSecrets account. "But we thought it was limited to the building. Now we're looking at a city-wide project. The building isn't the mystery—it's the key to the mystery."

Omnicorp Holdings has not responded to requests for comment. Corporate records list their address as a P.O. box that no longer exists. Their registered agent is a law firm that dissolved in 1987.

"Who is still buying property for a company with no visible leadership?" asked investigative journalist @FollowTheMoney. "Who has been executing a 72-year real estate plan? And why does it all point back to Hartwell?"

Notable properties in the spiral include:

- A warehouse at the spiral's outer edge containing, according to 311 complaints, "humming that never stops"
- A vacant lot that has resisted all development attempts since 1973 (equipment keeps malfunctioning)
- The defunct KXOM radio station, which broadcast until 1984 (its final broadcast was 8 hours of static followed by a voice saying "ready")
- The apartment building where Floor 7 mirrors the Hartwell Building's Floor 7 layout exactly

"Every property has something wrong with it," concluded u/MapperMayhem. "Not dangerous wrong. Just... wrong. And they're all connected. Literally. By geometry. Over 72 years. Someone is drawing something on this city, and we're just now seeing the outline."

The community is now mapping which addresses lie along the spiral lines between properties. Early reports suggest an unusual concentration of paranormal reports along these paths.

At press time, satellite imagery of the spiral had been removed from Gooble Maps. It has been replaced with imagery from 2019 that predates three of the purchases.
author: Sandra Mitchell, Local News
